title: Vercel AI SDK Masterclass: From Fundamentals to Deep Research

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary object is building an agentic deep-research workflow with multi-step agent loops, recursive planning, tool calling, and accumulated state management using the AI SDK. The AI SDK is a developer platform from Vercel and the deep research clone is a general-purpose agentic workflow not tied to a specific vertical. The workshop covers building the agent system from fundamentals and deploying it as a runnable terminal script. Requires JavaScript/Node.js familiarity and understanding of LLM APIs but provides guided step-by-step instruction. The session is a hands-on workshop with live coding demonstrations. All claims are grounded in direct transcript excerpts with said_in_transcript grade.

summary: Nico Albanese, who works on the AI SDK at Vercel, presents a workshop divided into fundamentals and building a deep research clone in Node.js. The fundamentals cover generateText (calling models with a prompt or messages array), the unified interface (switching providers by changing one line), tools/function calling (models generate structured tool calls, auto-invoking execute functions), and maxSteps for multi-step agent behavior. The unified interface is demonstrated by switching between OpenAI GPT-4o-mini, Perplexity sonar pro, and Google Gemini Flash 1.5. Tools are defined with name, description, parameters, and execute function, with the tool() utility providing type safety. maxSteps automatically sends tool results back to the model, looping until plain text or a step threshold. Parallel tool calls are demonstrated with weather lookups. Structured outputs are covered via generateText's experimental output option and the dedicated generateObject function, with Zod's .describe() for field-level instructions. The workshop then transitions to building a deep research clone: a terminal script that takes a query, conducts multi-step recursive research, and writes a markdown report. The workflow involves generating subqueries, searching the web for each, analyzing results for learnings and follow-up questions, and recursively going deeper while keeping accumulated research. Breadth and depth settings control scope and recursion depth. generateSearchQueries uses generateObject to produce search query strings. A searchWeb function uses the Exa API with livecrawl enabled, trimming irrelevant metadata to reduce tokens. searchAndProcess uses generateText with searchWeb and evaluate tools in a maxSteps loop (set to 5). The evaluate tool uses generateObject's enum mode (relevant/irrelevant). Search results are passed via local variables rather than tool parameters because crawled pages can be 10,000+ tokens. generateLearnings uses generateObject to extract a learning insight and follow-up questions. Recursion is implemented via a deepResearch function with depth and breadth parameters, a base case at depth zero, and accumulated research state. Source deduplication prevents reprocessing duplicate URLs by passing accumulated sources to the evaluate tool. Finally, a generateReport function uses generateText with o3-mini (a reasoning model preferred for synthesis) to create a report from accumulated research. The initial report lacked format guidance, so a system prompt is added to the generateResearch function, specifying a persona ('expert researcher'), today's date, markdown formatting, and research analyst guidelines. The improved report is structured, uses markdown, and contains detailed findings. The entire deep research clone is 218 lines of code.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: generateText is the foundational AI SDK primitive for calling language models, accepting either a prompt string or a messages array with role and content
The unified interface lets developers switch between model providers by changing a single line of code
maxSteps enables multi-step agent behavior by automatically sending tool results back to the model until plain text or the step threshold is reached
generateObject's enum mode provides ergonomic classification with restricted values, easier for the model than generating a full structured object
Passing long search results via local variables rather than tool parameters avoids costly, error-prone regeneration of existing context—faster, cheaper, more accurate
The deepResearch function implements recursion with depth/breadth parameters, a base case at depth zero, and accumulated research state passed through calls
Source deduplication prevents reprocessing duplicate URLs by passing accumulated sources to the evaluate tool, saving 10,000-20,000 tokens per duplicate

A generateReport function using a reasoning model (o3-mini) synthesizes accumulated research into a final report; a system prompt with persona, date, and formatting guidelines dramatically improves output quality
When working with language models, leave as little as possible for the model to infer—explicit system prompts with persona, format, and guidelines produce better results
The entire deep research clone fits in 218 lines of code, demonstrating the AI SDK's power for building sophisticated agentic workflows concisely

sections.title: Introduction and Setup
sections.summary: Nico introduces himself as working on the AI SDK at Vercel. The session is divided into fundamentals and building a deep research clone in Node.js. Setup involves cloning the repository, installing dependencies, copying environment variables, and running via a script alias.

sections.title: generateText Primitive
sections.summary: Introduces generateText as the first primitive, imported from the AI SDK. It takes a model specification and either a prompt string or a messages array with role and content. Demonstrated with GPT-4o-mini responding to 'hello world'.

sections.title: Unified Interface and Model Switching
sections.summary: Demonstrates the unified interface by showing GPT-4o-mini cannot answer about the 2025 AI Engineer Summit due to 2024 training cutoff. Switches to Perplexity sonar pro which returns correct results with sources accessible via the sources property. Also shows Google Gemini Flash 1.5 with search grounding.

sections.title: Tools and Function Calling
sections.summary: Introduces tools/function calling where the model receives a prompt plus available tools, each with name, description, parameters, and execute function. The tool() utility provides type safety between parameters and execute arguments. AI SDK auto-invokes execute functions and returns results in toolResults array.

sections.title: maxSteps and Multi-Step Agents
sections.summary: Introduces maxSteps property to enable multi-step agent behavior, automatically sending tool results back to the model for further generation until plain text is produced or the step threshold is reached. Steps can be inspected via result.steps.

sections.title: Parallel Tool Calls and Parameter Inference
sections.summary: Adds a get weather tool alongside the add numbers tool. The model makes parallel tool calls, fetching weather for San Francisco and New York simultaneously, then adding the temperatures. The model infers latitude and longitude from city names using its training data.

sections.title: Structured Outputs with generateText and generateObject
sections.summary: Introduces structured outputs. generateText's experimental output option uses Zod schemas. generateObject is introduced as a dedicated structured output function and the speaker's favorite. Zod's .describe() method provides field-level instructions, demonstrated with jargon-filled AI agent definitions.

sections.title: Deep Research Clone Introduction
sections.summary: Transitions to building a deep research clone as a terminal script. The workflow involves generating subqueries, searching the web for each, analyzing results for learnings and follow-up questions, and optionally going deeper. The companion site provides a natural language explanation and diagram.

sections.title: Recursive Research with Breadth and Depth
sections.summary: Explains the recursive nature of the deep research workflow: follow-up questions and existing research are used to generate new queries and repeat the process while keeping accumulated research. Breadth controls how many queries are generated at each step, and depth controls how many levels deep the research goes. Illustrated with an electric cars example.

sections.title: generateSearchQueries Function
sections.summary: Builds the generateSearchQueries function using generateObject with a main model specification. It takes a query string and a number of search queries (default 3), uses a template string prompt, and returns an array of strings via Zod schema (min 1, max 5). A main function is created with the prompt 'what do you need to be a D1 shotput athlete'.

sections.title: searchWeb Function with Exa API
sections.summary: Builds the searchWeb function using the Exa API with livecrawl enabled for up-to-date results, configured to return one result. Results are mapped to return only relevant fields, trimming metadata to reduce tokens sent to the model for cost savings and improved model effectiveness.

sections.title: searchAndProcess - Agentic Search and Evaluate Loop
sections.summary: Builds the most complex and agentic part: searchAndProcess. Uses generateText with searchWeb and evaluate tools, maxSteps set to 5. The evaluate tool uses generateObject's enum mode (relevant/irrelevant). Relevant results move to final search results; irrelevant ones are discarded.

sections.title: searchAndProcess Design Decisions and Execution
sections.summary: Explains enum mode ergonomics for two-value classification. If irrelevant, returns feedback string for the model to see in the next maxSteps iteration. Key design decision: search results passed via local variables, not tool parameters, because crawled pages can be 10,000 tokens—model would regenerate existing context (costly, slow, error-prone). Runs searchAndProcess showing irrelevant results triggering re-search and relevant results being kept.

sections.title: generateLearnings Function
sections.summary: Creates generateLearnings using generateObject to extract a learning insight (string) and follow-up questions (array of strings) from each relevant search result. Uses XML tags to nest stringified search result in the prompt. Running the pipeline generates learnings about D1 shotput requirements and follow-up questions.

sections.title: Recursive Deep Research with Accumulated State
sections.summary: Introduces recursion: take follow-up questions, create new query, call entire process again until satisfied with depth. Refactors logic into a deepResearch function with depth and breadth parameters. Defines Learning type (insight + follow-up questions) and Research type (accumulated state). Base case returns accumulated research when depth reaches zero. Otherwise combines follow-up questions and previous queries into a new prompt and calls itself with decremented depth and breadth.

sections.title: Source Deduplication in Evaluation
sections.summary: Identifies issue: model evaluating relevance lacks context of links already used in other steps, risking reprocessing the same 10,000-20,000 token source. Solution: pass accumulated source URLs to the evaluate tool in searchAndProcess. If URL already exists in existing results, mark as irrelevant. Only URLs (not full content) are stringified and passed via XML tags to save tokens.

sections.title: generateReport and System Prompt Enhancement
sections.summary: Creates generateReport function using generateText with o3-mini (a reasoning model preferred for synthesis) instead of the main model. Takes accumulated research, stringifies it in the prompt, and returns generated text. Main function is refactored to call generateReport and write the result to a markdown file using the fs module. First run produces a report after about a minute but lacks structure since no format guidance was given. Solution: a system prompt is added to the generateResearch function specifying a persona ('expert researcher'), today's date, markdown formatting, and research analyst guidelines. Second run produces a much more structured markdown report with detailed D1 shotput findings (55ft benchmark, 60ft for elite recruits, four years varsity). The entire deep research clone is 218 lines of code. Nico closes with contact info and thanks.

limitations: GPT-4o-mini cannot access the web and has a 2024 training data cutoff
Manually handling tool results with conditional statements is error-prone and does not scale with many tools
When a model generates a tool call, result.text is empty, requiring additional handling to get synthesized text
Parameter inference from context (like inferring latitude/longitude from city names) is not recommended for production use in this particular example
The deep research clone is a simplified terminal implementation, not a full application
searchWeb returns only 1 result per query in the demo; should be configurable in production
livecrawl on Exa API takes a performance/time hit compared to cached results
maxSteps for the agentic loop is kept relatively low (5) to avoid the agent going off track
Using tool parameters to parse long search results forces the model to regenerate existing context, costing money and time and being error-prone
Without source deduplication, the model may reprocess the same URL across recursive steps, wasting significant tokens
The first report generation gave the model no guidance on report format, requiring the model to infer structure, which produced less structured output
Model choice for report generation should be experimented with; o3-mini was found to work well but users should try different models
